title: Start from Home
summary: Choose a destination and a layout, then your photos, and adjust the pages before you create the project.

sections.heading: Choose a destination and layout
steps: Open Home. On iPhone, Home is the first tab in the bar at the bottom, beside Templates and Projects. On iPad, it is in the sidebar.

Tap a destination at the top of Home, such as Post 3:4, Post 4:5, Story, Threads, or Video. Each one shows its page shape beside the name. Tap More (…) for every destination. Choosing one here does not change your saved default.
Where the page can turn, choose Vertical or Horizontal below the destinations. Stories, TV, and square pages already have a fixed shape.
Home lists Favorites, Smart layouts, Layouts, and Camera Details Designs. Each row scrolls sideways, and each card shows sample pages in the page’s own shape.
Tap a layout, such as One Photo, Two Photos, Four Photos, Gallery Print, Panorama, Strip, or Contact Sheet, then choose your photos.
shots: Home on iPhone: destination choices, smart layouts, and layouts.

sections.heading: Adjust the pages before you create
steps: Decks shows your pages right away. The current page is large, a strip below shows every page, and the title shows the count, such as 5 photos · 3 pages.
Tap a page in the strip to see it. Tap Change Photos to pick a different set.
Use the tools at the bottom: Layout, Frame, and Camera. Each opens a panel over the pages; tap the tool again or Close to hide it. On a wide iPad, the panel sits beside the pages.

Layout switches to another layout, with smart layouts first. It also holds Photos per Page for one-photo and smart layouts, Photo Arrangement (Side by Side or Stacked) for two-photo layouts, and Panels for a panorama.
Frame sets the Border and Background, and Depth for Gallery Print. Camera turns on Camera Details and chooses which details show.
With more than one photo, choose All Photos or This Photo (All Pages or This Page for layouts with several photos) to decide what your change applies to.
Tap Create to open the project in the editor. You can change everything there.
shots: Every page on one screen, with the page strip and tools.
The Layout panel with Photos per Page.

sections.heading: Put photos on shared pages
steps: In Layout, Photos per Page offers One, 2, 3, or Grid of 4. With 2 or 3, choose Stacked or Side by Side. Photos shaped across the page share a page; photos shaped like the page keep a page each.
Turn on Only if taken within 10 minutes to share a page only between photos taken close together.

Under the pages, Split Page gives each photo on the current page its own page. Join with Next puts the current page’s photos with the next page’s. You can also drag a page in the strip onto another page to join them. A page holds up to four photos.
shots: Select a shared page to split it or join it with the next page.

sections.heading: Your destinations
steps: Setup chooses which destinations appear at the top of Home. Skip Setup opens the full catalog with a 3:4 starting canvas.
Settings → Destinations lets you add destinations and photo frames. Run Setup Again revisits your choices.
Settings → Start Page chooses whether Decks opens to Home, Templates, or Projects.

sections.heading: Arrange your layouts
steps: Touch and hold a card in Layouts, then drag it to a new position, or choose Move Earlier or Move Later. Decks remembers that order on your other devices.
Choose Favorite in the same menu to add a layout to Favorites at the top of Home. Remove Favorite takes it off.

macSections.heading: Choose a destination and layout
steps: Click Home in the sidebar, or press ⌘1. Choose a size from the menu at the top, and Vertical or Horizontal beside it. Changing the size here does not change your saved default.
Home lists Favorites, Smart layouts, Layouts, and Camera Details Designs. Click a layout, or Control-click it and choose Use This Layout.
Choose your photos from your Photos library and click Continue, or click Choose Files… to pick files in Finder.

macSections.heading: Adjust the pages before you create
steps: Decks shows the current page large, with Page 1 of 3 and arrows below it, and a strip of every page. The bar at the bottom shows the count, such as 5 photos · 3 pages.

Choose Layout, Frame, or Camera at the top of the panel on the right. Layout changes the layout, Photos per Page, and Photo Arrangement. Frame sets the Border, Background, and Depth. Camera turns on Camera Details and chooses the details.
With more than one photo, Frame and Camera offer All Photos or This Photo (All Pages or This Page) to decide what your change applies to.
On shared pages, Split Page and Join with Next sit under the strip. Drag a page onto another to join them.
Click Create Project to open the project in the editor, or Cancel to go back to Home.

macSections.heading: Your destinations
steps: Setup narrows the size menu to the destinations you choose. Skip Setup shows every size instead.
Use the size menu at the top of Home to try another size. Custom Size… makes any shape between 1:10 and 10:1.
Edit Destinations… in the size menu opens Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ Destinations. Add destinations and photo frames, choose a default, or Run Setup Again…, then click Save Changes.

macSections.heading: Two-photo arrangements
steps: For Two Photos, choose Side by Side or Stacked under Photo Arrangement in the Layout panel.
In the editor, open Layout and turn Vertical Pair on or off to change it later.

macSections.heading: Arrange your starting layouts
steps: Drag a card in Layouts to a new position, or Control-click it and choose Move Earlier or Move Later. Decks remembers that order on your other devices.
Control-click a layout and choose Favorite to add it to Favorites at the top of Home.

ipadShots: Home on iPad, with your library in the sidebar.

title: Smart Layout for Aura frames
summary: Prepare vertical and horizontal photos together for a digital frame, then choose which photos appear in each pair.

sections.heading: Choose your frame
steps: In Settings → Destinations, choose Add a Photo Frame. Select your Aura model and orientation.

On Home, tap your frame at the top. Home shows Frame layouts sized for it: Smart Layout first, then Two Side by Side (Two Stacked on an upright frame), Soft Background, Full Screen, and Thin Border. More Layouts shows the rest; Fewer Layouts hides them again.
Tap Smart Layout and select the photos you want to prepare together.
shots: Aura Carver chosen on Home, with Smart Layout first under Frame layouts.

sections.heading: Review the automatic arrangement
steps: Decks shows the pages right away, with a strip of every page below.
For a landscape frame, vertical photos are paired two to a page and horizontal photos get their own pages. An unmatched vertical photo gets a soft background. Square photos get their own pages.
For an upright frame, horizontal photos are stacked in pairs and vertical photos get their own pages.
Within each group, Decks starts in capture-date order when dates are available. This is an arrangement by photo shape, not face recognition or subject matching.
shots: The Layout panel shows the vertical pairs and the horizontal photo.

sections.heading: Choose the pairs and their look
steps: Tap Layout in the tools at the bottom. Under Vertical Pairs (Horizontal Pairs on an upright frame), tap two photos to swap them, or drag one onto another. You choose which photos belong together.

Choose White or Black for the pair background. Under Horizontal Photos (Vertical Photos on an upright frame), choose White Border, Black Border, or Fill for the individual pages. A black border blends into the frame’s own black edge, so the photo looks like part of the frame; a white border or soft background reads as a background behind the photo. Fill crops the photo a little to cover the screen; check faces and edges.
If your photos suit another frame layout better, Layout suggests it. Choose Use to switch, or Keep to stay with Smart Layout.
Tap Create and review the crop on each page in the editor. You can continue editing the result.
shots: Tap a photo to move it.
Tap another photo to swap them.

sections.heading: Share to Aura
steps: In the editor, tap Export, then tap Share and choose Aura. The Aura app uploads the pages to your frame.
To keep a copy first, tap Save to Photos, then add the images in the Aura app.
A paired Decks page is one exported image, so the two photos stay together instead of being left to Aura’s automatic pairing. Decks does not sign in to your Aura account.
Save a design you like as a template. To sort another mixed batch by photo shape, start Smart Layout again.
shots: Choose Aura in the share sheet. Suggested contacts are blurred in this screenshot.

sections.heading: Smart layouts for other destinations
steps: For any other destination, Home’s Smart layouts row offers Singles & Pairs, Singles & Threes, and Singles & Fours. Photos shaped like the page get a page each; photos shaped across it share a page, two, three, or four at a time.
Build Your Own, at the end of that row, makes a smart layout with your own rules. See Build your own smart layout.

macSections.heading: Start a mixed batch
steps: Open Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ Destinations ▸ Add a Photo Frame…. Select your frame and orientation, click Done, then Save Changes.
Open Home (⌘1) and choose the frame from the size menu. Frame layouts lists Smart Layout first. Click it, then choose your photos from Photos and click Continue, or click Choose Files….

macSections.heading: Review, swap, and finish
steps: Open Layout in the panel on the right. It shows Vertical Pairs and Horizontal Photos for a landscape frame, or Horizontal Pairs and Vertical Photos for an upright frame. An unmatched photo in the pairing group uses a soft background.
Click two photos to swap them, or drag one onto another. Choose White or Black for pairs and White Border, Black Border, or Fill for individual pages.
Click Create Project, review the pages, and use File ▸ Export… to save images to Photos or a folder. Then add them in the Aura app. The same grouping and crop considerations apply on Mac.

macSections.heading: Smart layouts for other destinations
steps: For other sizes, Home’s Smart layouts row offers Singles & Pairs, Singles & Threes, and Singles & Fours. Click Build Your Own to make your own rules.

title: Build your own smart layout
summary: Choose which photos get their own page and which share one, then save the rules as a template.

sections.heading: Open the builder
steps: On Home, scroll to the end of Smart layouts and tap Build Your Own.
Or open Templates and tap Smart Layout. On iPad, Templates also has New Smart Layout in the toolbar.
To change a smart layout you saved, touch and hold it in Templates and choose Edit Smart Layout. Your changes keep its page shape.

sections.heading: Set the rules
steps: Page chooses the page shape from your destinations, as on Home.

Under Photos, the photos shaped like the page get their own page. For the photos shaped across it, choose how they share a page: Stacked, 2; Stacked, 3; Side by Side, 2; Side by Side, 3; or Grid of 4. Square photos get their own page.
Turn on Only if taken within 10 minutes to share a page only between photos taken close together.

sections.heading: Choose the look and camera details
steps: Under Look, choose a Background (Photo Blur, White, or Black) and a Border (None, Auto, White, or Black).
Turn on Use for New Photos to make this smart layout the default for Add Photos & Videos and Photos → Share → Decks.
Turn on Camera Details and choose which details show. For a saved smart layout, choose the details later in the editor’s Camera tool.

sections.heading: Preview and save
steps: The pages at the top change as you choose. Preview With switches between Samples and My Photos. My Photos asks you to pick photos; Choose Others picks a different set. Your photos are used only for the preview.
Tap Save and name the smart layout. Decks suggests a name that describes the rules, such as Singles & Threes.
Your smart layout appears under Smart Layouts in Templates. Tap it and choose Use Template to lay out new photos, or mark it as a favorite to show it in Favorites on Home.

macSections.heading: Open the builder
steps: On Home, click Build Your Own at the end of Smart layouts. Or click Templates in the sidebar (⌘3), then New Smart Layout.
To change one you saved, Control-click it in Templates and choose Edit Smart Layout.

macSections.heading: Set the rules and look
steps: Page chooses the page shape from your destinations.

Under Photos, the photos shaped like the page get their own page. Choose how the others share a page: Stacked, 2; Stacked, 3; Side by Side, 2; Side by Side, 3; or Grid of 4. Square photos get their own page. Only if taken within 10 minutes limits sharing to photos taken close together.
Under Look, choose a Background and Border. Use for New Photos makes this smart layout your New Project Template.
Turn on Camera Details and choose which details show.

macSections.heading: Preview and save
steps: Preview With switches the pages at the top between Samples and My Photos. Choose Others picks a different set of your photos. The copies are for the preview only and are removed when the builder closes.
Click Save… and name the smart layout, or click Cancel to close without saving. It appears under Smart Layouts in Templates.

title: Start with your photos
summary: Skip the layouts and build as you go.

sections.heading: Add photos or videos
steps: On iPhone, tap the round + button beside the tab bar (Add Photos & Videos). On iPad, tap Add Photos & Videos in the toolbar. It is available on Home, Templates, and Projects.
Select your photos or clips, then confirm your selection. Decks opens a project using your New Project Defaults.
Open Layout to choose the page shape and arrangement. Open Frame to choose None if you want a borderless start, then add styling when you need it.

sections.heading: Choose your defaults
steps: In Settings → New Project Defaults, choose the template and layout used for this route and for Photos → Share → Decks.
Editing a project does not change those defaults. A smart layout with Use for New Photos on becomes the default template.

sections.heading: Add more later
steps: Use Add Photos in the editor to bring in more images. New photos follow the project’s layout and fill available photo slots before adding pages.
Videos come from clips you choose to import. Adding a still photo does not turn it into a moving video.

macSections.heading: Add photos or videos
steps: Choose File ▸ Import Photos and Videos… (⌘O), drag files from Finder onto the Decks window, or paste them with ⌘V.
To use your Photos library, click Photos in the sidebar, select photos or clips, and click the Add button. Decks opens a project using your New Project Template.
Open Layout in the inspector to choose the page size and arrangement. Open Frame and choose None if you want a borderless start, then add styling when you need it.
File ▸ New Blank Project starts with an empty page instead.

macSections.heading: Choose your defaults
steps: In Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ General, choose the New Project Template used for imports and pasted photos. You can also Control-click a template and choose Set as Default.
Editing a project does not change that default.

macSections.heading: Add more later
steps: With a project open, choose File ▸ Add Photos and Videos… (⇧⌘O) or Add from Photos Library…, or drag files onto the editor. Each new photo gets its own page at the end.
To lay out new photos like a saved design, choose File ▸ Add Pages from Template… instead.
Videos come from clips you choose to import. Adding a still photo does not turn it into a moving video.

title: Move around the editor
summary: Selection, pages, gestures, and getting Home.

sections.heading: Browse and select
steps: Swipe left or right from the empty canvas margin to change pages. Swipe up from that margin to arrange pages; swipe down to hide details. Customize these actions in Settings → Editor → Gestures, or Gestures in the page menu. Pinch to look closer, then tap Fit to return to the whole page.

Tap a photo, text, logo, or camera details to select it. A blue dashed outline identifies your selection without adding a border to the exported artwork. Drag to move it. Tap Done to return to browsing. In Freeform, pinch and rotate a selected photo. Photo opens its Crop section; switch to Layer for placement and effects.

Use Select Item for small or overlapping objects. Select text, then tap Edit Text to write. Dragging a fixed-layout photo adjusts it inside its frame; Photo → Position → Move Freely converts just that page to Freeform.
With Snap to Guides on in Project Options, dragged text, logos, camera details, and Freeform photos line up with the page, photos, borders, and other items. A blue guide shows what they caught.

Tap Arrange beside the canvas to place the photo left, right, top, or bottom alongside its text and camera details. Cards grow to fit with room around them. Changing the photo or page shape updates the arrangement. Undo restores the whole change.
Tap Done to leave the selection and browse again. Open the page indicator for Previous, Next, and Arrange Pages.

sections.heading: Find your tools
steps: The bottom tool strip opens Layout, Frame, Photo, Text, Camera, Stamp, and Caption. Tap the current drawer’s tool again to hide or show it; tap another tool to switch its controls. Tap a section’s chevron to reveal more controls.

Details initially fit the controls in each tool. Drag the handle to choose a height for that tool; the photo continuously fits the space above it. Reset panel sizes in Settings → Editor. Tap the active tool to hide its controls and give the photo more room; tap it again to return.

This Page or All Pages stays beside the details handle across editing tools and remembers your choice as you select objects or browse pages. It controls page layout and frame settings; Photo, Text, Camera, and Stamp controls edit their selected item.
Hold a tool to rearrange, remove, or add tools. Settings → Editor → Reset Tool Strip restores the original tools.

Canvas controls start hidden to give the photo more room. Tap the small Show Controls button at the top right to open the icon rail; the chevron hides it again. The sidebar keeps selection, arrangement, and other object actions. Open Photo in the bottom tool strip for crop, sizing, position, replacement, layers, and clip controls.
Open Photo and choose Shape for Original, square, or portrait ratios. Switch Orientation turns the shape sideways. This changes only that photo inside its slot; Layout changes the page.

Crop opens a large workspace. Choose a ratio or Free, drag the edges or crop area, and pinch to refine. Apply saves one undoable edit; Cancel leaves the photo unchanged. Reset Shape restores the layout’s original shape.

sections.heading: Return Home
steps: Tap Home in the editor to save and return to Projects. Reopen the project there to keep editing.
Saving a reusable template takes you to Templates. Leaving the start screen before you tap Create returns to Home.

macSections.heading: Browse and select
steps: Double-click a project to open it. Press ← or → to change pages, or Home and End for the first and last page. You can also click a page in the strip under the canvas.

Click a photo, text, or camera details on the canvas to select it. An outline shows your selection without adding a border to the exported artwork. Drag to move it; in a fixed layout, dragging a photo moves it inside its frame.

With Snap to Guides on (Layout ▸ Guides in the inspector), dragged text, logos, camera details, and Freeform photos line up with the page, photos, borders, and other items, and a blue guide shows what they caught. A logo’s center can lock onto a photo’s border line or into a corner where two borders meet.
⌘-click or ⇧-click to select several items, then drag them together or press Delete to remove them. Option-arrow keys nudge the selection a little at a time.
Drag the small square at the lower-right corner of selected text or a freeform photo to resize it.
Press Esc to leave the selection. Press it again to fit the canvas, and once more to return to Projects.

macSections.heading: Zoom and view
steps: Press ⌘= to zoom in, ⌘- to zoom out, and ⌘0 to fit the page. Press Z to switch between the whole page and a closer look.
Press Tab or ⌘I to hide the inspector and give the page more room; press it again to bring the controls back. On a video page, Space previews the clip and plays or pauses it.
Control-click the canvas for Add Text, Duplicate Selection, Undo, Redo, and Fit Canvas.

macSections.heading: Find your tools
steps: The inspector on the right has Layout, Frame, Photo, Text, Camera, Stamp, and Caption. Click a tool to see its controls. The ⓘ button opens Photo Details for the selected photo.

The All Pages or This Page menu under the tools decides whether Layout and Frame changes apply to every page or only this one. Photo, Text, and Camera controls edit the selected item. Stamp has its own Apply to menu.

Photo ▸ Crop sets Fit or Fill, Zoom, and position, and offers Center, Move to New Page, Move to Page, and Replace Photo…. Freeform photos also show Freeform Layer controls for size, rotation, and order.
Press ⌘K for the command palette. Type part of a command’s name, then press Return. Pin the commands you use most with ⇧⌘P.
Menus show each keyboard shortcut. Change them in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… (⌘/). Control-click the toolbar to customize its buttons. Click the project name in the toolbar to rename it.

macSections.heading: Return to your library
steps: Click Back to Projects in the toolbar, or press ⌘[. Decks keeps your changes; reopen the project in Projects to continue.
⌘1 through ⌘5 go to Home, Projects, Templates, Photos, and Recent Activity.
Keep projects side by side in separate windows: choose File ▸ New Window (⇧⌘N), or Control-click a project and choose Open in New Window.

title: Borders, backgrounds & depth
summary: None, Plain, Film, and Gallery Print shadows.

sections.heading: Choose a border
steps: Before you create a project, open Frame in the start screen’s tools. In the editor, open Frame. Choose None, Plain, or Film where supported.
Plain gives you border color and thickness. None removes the frame. Switching styles remembers your settings so you can compare them.

Change the background separately from the border. Background → Color includes White, Black, Ivory, colors sampled from the selected photo, and a custom picker. Choose Photo or Video to replace the background image or clip.

sections.heading: Film edges
steps: Choose Film, then tap a stock preview and adjust the border width. Film is a frame choice; Strip and Contact Sheet remain layouts.
Open Film Options for the format, sprockets, edge lettering, and other film details. Choose stock lettering or your own text.
New film borders fit around your current photo proportions and crop. Older film projects keep their original appearance.

sections.heading: Add depth
steps: Gallery Print offers a shadow before you create the project. In the start screen’s Frame tool, turn on Shadow under Depth and adjust Shadow Strength to lift the photo from the background.
In the editor, open Frame → Depth to adjust the shadow. Double-tap an adjustment slider or use its Reset control to return to the template’s starting value.

macSections.heading: Choose a border
steps: In the start screen’s Frame tool, or Frame ▸ Border in the editor’s inspector, choose None, Plain, or Film where supported.
Plain gives you border color and width. On the start screen, choose Auto, White, Black, or Custom, then set Frame Thickness. None removes the frame.

Change the background separately from the border. On the start screen, choose Black, White, Photo Blur, or Custom Color. In the editor, Frame ▸ Background offers Automatic, Color, or Image, Choose Background Photo…, and Blur, Brightness, Saturation, and Scale.

macSections.heading: Film edges
steps: Choose Film, then pick a Stock and Format and adjust the border Width. Film is a frame choice; Strip and Contact Sheet remain layouts.
Type Edge Text to replace the stock lettering with your own words.

macSections.heading: Add depth
steps: Gallery Print offers a shadow before you create the project. In the start screen’s Frame tool, turn on Shadow and adjust Shadow Strength to lift the photo from the background.
In the editor, open Frame ▸ Depth for Shadow, Shadow Blur, and Shadow Opacity, or turn on Outline.

title: Camera details & Halide credits
summary: Add camera details to a photo, choose where they sit, and style them.

sections.heading: Add camera details
steps: Before you create a project, open Camera in the start screen’s tools and turn on Camera Details. In the editor, open Camera and switch Camera Details on for the selected photo.
Or start from a Camera Details Design on Home: Gear Band, Wall Label, Spec Sheet, Film Strip, Corner Mark, Spine, or Details List. Each is a finished page built around the camera and exposure.

To restyle pages you already have, open Templates in the editor (Templates… in the page menu at the top on iPhone, or Templates in the toolbar on iPad). Under Designs, choose This Page or All Pages, then tap a design. Your photos and words stay; the page takes the design’s look.

sections.heading: Choose where the details sit
steps: Placement puts the details Under, Above, or to the Side of the photo (Left or Right), On Photo, or Free. Under, Above, and Side place the details in the page margin, and the photo moves to make room.
Drag the details anywhere. Drop them in a margin to snap them there, or leave them where you drop them on the photo.
If there isn’t room beside a small photo, the details sit on it, and the panel says why. Try a smaller Size. Details on a film border, a panorama, or a Freeform page also sit on the photo.
Size sets how large the details are.
shots: The camera details card: Styles, Placement, Size, and Shows.

sections.heading: Choose what they show
steps: Shows lists the lines on the card. Switch a line on or off, or reorder the lines. More Details… opens the photo’s full list, where you can add or edit any detail.

For Fujifilm photos, turn on Fujifilm Recipe to add the recorded film simulation and settings. Choose Card, Line, Dials, or Film Box for how they look. Settings the photo does not record are listed under Not Recorded on This Photo; tap Add to enter a value you know.
If the photo also has a separate Fujifilm card from an earlier version, Move into Camera Details shows that recipe with the camera details, in their look and place.

sections.heading: Style and saved styles
steps: Open Style for Arrangement, Type, Ink, and Background. Type uses the design’s own fonts by Default; Fonts… lets you choose any family, with open-source families listed first. Ink is Auto, Light, or Dark.
Background is the Look’s Own, None, or a Plate with its own color, opacity, and corners.
On a 9:16 page, Keep Inside Stories Safe Area keeps the details clear of the areas Instagram draws over. New details on a Story page start with it on.
Styles, at the top of the panel, lists your saved styles. Tap one to use it on the selected details. Save Style saves how these details look and where they sit, for any page.
Details from earlier versions keep their own controls. Use the New Camera Details converts them to the current card.

sections.heading: Halide credits
steps: For a Shot with Halide credit, tap it to open its controls. Change its wording, adjust its spacing and width, or remove its background.
The Halide logo and text move as a group, so you don’t need to line them up separately.

sections.heading: Remove details
steps: Switch Camera Details off, or choose Remove Details from the Camera panel’s actions.
Removing the last camera card recenters a single photo when no text or logo remains. Undo restores both the card and its arrangement.

sections.heading: When details are missing
steps: Decks can only read the metadata included in the imported file. Screenshots and photos saved by other apps may be missing camera or exposure information.
Try the original photo, or use Settings → My Gear & Places and Custom Variables for information you want to supply yourself.

Save your Fujifilm recipes in Settings → Fujifilm Recipes, then apply one in Photo Details. A saved recipe supplies its name and settings even when automatic detection is unavailable. Applying a recipe adds information; it does not change the photo’s colors.

macSections.heading: Add camera details
steps: Before you create a project, choose Camera at the top of the start screen’s panel and turn on Camera Details. In the editor, open Camera in the inspector and turn on Camera Details for the current photo.
Use Apply To to place the same details on the Selected Photo, All Photos on Page, or one Shared Page card.

To restyle pages with a Camera Details Design, Control-click a page in the page strip and choose Apply Design or Apply Design to All Pages. The Templates menu in the toolbar also lists the designs under Apply Design to This Page.

macSections.heading: Placement, size, and style
steps: Placement puts the details Under, Above, or to the Side of the photo (Left or Right), On Photo, or Free. Under, Above, and Side place the details in the page margin.
Drag the details on the canvas; drop them in a margin to snap them there. Arrow keys nudge them.
Shows lists the lines on the card. Turn lines on or off, reorder them, or click More Details… to add or edit a detail.
For Fujifilm photos, turn on Fujifilm Recipe and choose Card, Line, Dials, or Film Box. Settings the photo does not record are listed under Not Recorded on This Photo.

Open Style for Arrangement, Type (Default or Fonts…, open-source families first), Ink, Background (Look’s Own, None, or Plate), and Keep Inside Stories Safe Area on 9:16 pages. Styles lists your saved styles; Save Style keeps the current look for any page.

macSections.heading: Remove details
steps: Remove Card takes the details off the page. Undo (⌘Z) brings them back.

macSections.heading: When details are missing
steps: Decks can only read the metadata included in the imported file. Screenshots and photos saved by other apps may be missing camera or exposure information.
Try the original photo, or click ⓘ in the inspector. Under Edit Photo Details, choose a category and type the values, or choose Apply Saved Gear.
Save cameras, lenses, film, and processing in Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ My Gear. Match EXIF Names uses your names for every photo with that EXIF wording.

Save your Fujifilm recipes in Settings ▸ Recipes, then choose the Camera category in Photo Details and use Apply Film Recipe. Applying a recipe adds information; it does not change the photo’s colors.

title: Add a date stamp
summary: Print the date, time, place, or a short note on a photo.

sections.heading: Turn on the stamp
steps: Select a photo and tap Stamp in the tool strip, between Camera and Caption. Switch Stamp on. The stamp sits in the photo’s bottom-right corner, inside its frame.

Set All Lines picks one style for every line: Film, Digital, Clean, or Typewriter. Film has the orange glow of a film camera’s date imprint and starts a little translucent. Each line can also have its own style.

Use the menu at the top of the panel to choose what your changes apply to: This Photo, This Page, Selected Pages, or All Photos. Only the setting you change is applied; each photo keeps the rest. In Arrange, select pages and tap Edit Stamps to change only those pages.
New stamps start with the last style you used.
shots: The Stamp panel: styles and the lines on the stamp.

sections.heading: Choose the lines
steps: Below the styles is a list of lines: Date, Time, Place, and Note. Each shows what it prints on this photo. Tap the circle beside a line to show or hide it.

Tap a line in the list, or the line on the photo, to open its own editor: its style, Color, Size, Opacity, Shadow, and Background. Reset puts that line back as it started. Tap Stamp at the top of the editor to return to the list.
Drag a line on the photo to move it on its own, or use its Horizontal and Vertical sliders. Back to Stack puts it with the other lines again.
Horizontal and Vertical run from one corner of the photo to the other. Tap a slider’s number to type a value.
Note prints a few words you type. With several photos chosen, the same note goes on each one.

sections.heading: Dates and times
steps: Decks stamps the date the photo was taken (Capture Date). Choose Custom Date to stamp a different one, such as the date of a scanned print.
Only the stamp changes. Your photo and its saved date stay the same.
In the Date line’s editor, Order sets Y M D, M D Y, or D M Y.
Time prints the time the photo was taken. If a photo has no capture date, choose Custom Date to stamp one.
shots: The Date line: capture date or a custom date, and the date order.

sections.heading: Places
steps: Turn on Place to print where the photo was taken. Decks reads the location saved in the photo, then asks Apple Maps for a name such as “Louisville, KY.” Only the photo’s coordinates are sent.
In Place’s editor, Show chooses how much prints: a landmark, the city, the city and state, or the country, each written as it reads for that photo.
Tap the place to open the place editor. Type a name, or choose Look Up on the Map to search or move the pin. Use the Photo’s Own Place goes back to the name from the photo.
Decks asks for your location only if you tap Current Location on the map, to center it where you are. Your location is not tracked or stored.
Turn on Save as Favorite to reuse a name, such as Home, with one tap; favorites appear under Place. A favorite with a spot on the map can also use Name Every Photo Taken Here.
Edit or forget favorites in Settings → Favorite Places. Favorite places sync through iCloud and never change your photos.
If a photo has no location saved, type a name or look the place up. Location may have been off for Camera, or it was removed when the photo was shared.
Exported photos keep their GPS location only if you turn on Include Location when exporting. The stamp shows only the place name.

sections.heading: Position and remove
steps: Under Position, choose a Corner: Bottom Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Center, Top Right, or Top Left.
Drag the stamp anywhere on the page, even off the photo. Near a corner, it snaps back in. Snap to Corner returns a moved stamp to its corner.
Sideways on Vertical Photos runs the date down the left edge of vertical photos.
To take a stamp off, switch Stamp off, or select the stamp on the page and choose Remove Stamp.

macSections.heading: Turn on the stamp
steps: Click a photo, click Stamp in the inspector, and switch Stamp on in the Date Stamp section. The stamp sits in the photo’s bottom-right corner, inside its frame. Drag it anywhere on the page; near a corner it snaps back in. Arrow keys nudge it.
Set All Lines picks one style for every line: Film, Digital, Clean, or Typewriter. Each line can also have its own style.

Use Apply to at the top of the Date Stamp section to change This Photo, This Page, or All Photos at once. Select several pages in the page strip to change only those. Only the setting you change is applied; each photo keeps the rest.

macSections.heading: Choose the lines
steps: The list shows Date, Time, Place, and Note, with what each prints on this photo. The checkbox shows or hides a line.

Click Edit…, or click the line on the photo, to open its own editor: Style, Color, Size, Opacity, Shadow, Background, Horizontal, and Vertical. Reset puts that line back as it started. Click Stamp at the top to return to the list.
Drag a line to move it on its own; Back to Stack puts it with the others. Click a slider’s number to type a value.

macSections.heading: Dates and places
steps: Date uses Capture Date. Choose Custom Date to stamp a different one. Only the stamp changes; your photo and its saved date stay the same. Order sets Y M D, M D Y, or D M Y.
Place prints a name from the photo’s saved location, looked up with Apple Maps. Only the photo’s coordinates are sent. Show chooses how much of the name prints.
Click Edit Place… to type a name or look it up on the map. Turn on Save as Favorite to reuse a name, then choose it from the menu beside Place. Edit favorites in Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ Favorite Places.
Decks asks for your location only if you click Current Location on the map. Exported photos keep their GPS location only if you turn on Include Location when exporting.

macSections.heading: Position and remove
steps: Open Position for Corner, Snap to Corner, and Sideways on Vertical Photos.
To take a stamp off, turn Stamp off, or select the stamp and press Delete. Control-click it and choose Remove Stamp to do the same.

title: Text, logos & variables
summary: Put words and reusable information on a page.

sections.heading: Add text or a logo
steps: Use Text in the editor or the add menu to place text on the page. Tap the text to select it, then tap Edit Text to change its wording. Adjust its appearance in the text controls.
Manage reusable logos in Settings → My Logos. Use the editor’s Logo tool to place one in a design.

To hold a logo on a photo’s corner, tap a Photo Corner button under Position, or drag the logo onto the corner of the photo’s border. It follows the photo when you move it, and the photo shrinks a little, evenly on both sides, so the whole logo stays inside the page margins. Drag the logo anywhere to let it go.
With Snap to Guides on in Project Options, dragged text and logos line up with the page, photos, borders, and other items. A blue guide shows what they caught.
Text on the canvas becomes part of the exported image. Use Caption for posting text that you want to copy separately.

sections.heading: Insert photo information
steps: Type ; at the start of a word in a supported text or caption field to open the variable picker. Choose the information you want to insert.
Photo variables use information from the current image. Set up your own values in Settings → Custom Variables, or add gear and places in My Gear & Places.
Check the resolved text when changing photos. An image without the requested metadata cannot fill that value automatically.

macSections.heading: Add text or a logo
steps: Choose Edit ▸ Add Text (⇧⌘T), or open Text in the inspector and click Add Text. Type in the text box there, then click Text Style… to change its appearance.
Set Horizontal, Vertical, Width, and Alignment, or use Align to Page or Photo. Duplicate (⌘D) and Remove are in the same section.
Click Add Logo… to place an image file, such as your logo, on the page.

To hold a logo on a photo’s corner, click a Photo Corner button in the inspector, or drag the logo onto a corner where two borders meet. It follows the photo when you move it, and the photo shrinks a little, evenly on both sides, so the whole logo stays inside the page margins. Drag the logo anywhere to let it go.
Text on the canvas becomes part of the exported image. Use Caption for posting text that you want to copy separately.

macSections.heading: Reuse photo information
steps: Camera details fill in from each photo’s metadata. Edit any line in Camera when you want different wording.
Set up your own cameras, lenses, and film in Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ My Gear so they fill in the same way every time.
Check the details when changing photos. An image without the requested metadata cannot fill that value automatically.

title: Adjust, reset & undo
summary: Restore the starting look without losing your place.

sections.heading: Reset one adjustment
steps: Drag a slider to change a value. Double-tap the slider to reset it, or use its visible Reset control.
With VoiceOver, select the adjustment and use its Reset action. All three methods restore the same value.

Reset returns to the selected template’s baseline. If the template has no value for that control, Decks uses the control’s initial default. Ordinary edits and reopening the project do not redefine that starting point.

sections.heading: Undo a change
steps: Use Undo in the editor to reverse an edit, including a reset. Redo reapplies a change you have undone.
Reset one adjustment when you only want to restore that setting; other edits stay in place.

macSections.heading: Change or reset an adjustment
steps: Drag a slider to change a value, or type an exact value in the field beside it and press Return.
In Layout ▸ Guides, Reset Page clears this page’s own changes so it follows the All Pages settings again.
Edit ▸ Reset Layout… returns every page to how it was before your first layout change in this session. You can undo it.
On the start screen, Reset beside Frame Thickness or Shadow Strength returns that slider to the layout’s starting value.

macSections.heading: Undo a change
steps: Choose Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z) to reverse an edit, including a reset. Redo (⇧⌘Z) reapplies a change you have undone. Both are in the toolbar, too.
Reset only what you need; other edits stay in place.

title: Panoramas for a carousel
summary: Split a photo into panels and preview the swipe.

sections.heading: Set up the panels
steps: Choose Panorama on Home and add your photo. In the start screen’s Layout tool, set Panels to the number of linked panels, from 2 to 6.
In the editor, open Layout and tap Preview Panorama to see adjacent rounded panels in a horizontally scrolling preview, like a Threads carousel.
In an existing project, the editor’s options also offer Split Photo into Panorama Panels.

sections.heading: Export and post in order
steps: Open Export and check the panorama preview. Export all the panels you want to share.
In Threads or Instagram, select the exported images in their panel order to build the carousel. Decks prepares the files; you choose and publish the post in the destination app.

macSections.heading: Set up the panels
steps: Choose Panorama on Home and pick your photo. In the Layout panel, set the number of linked panels, from 2 to 6.
In an existing project, select a photo and choose Edit ▸ Split Panorama into 3 Pages, or click the same button in Layout.
Panels stay together when you select, duplicate, or delete pages in the page strip.

macSections.heading: Export and post in order
steps: Choose File ▸ Export…. Each panel becomes its own image, in order.
In Threads or Instagram, select the exported images in their panel order to build the carousel. Decks prepares the files; you choose and publish the post in the destination app.

title: Create your own template
summary: Save a reusable design, then try it with new photos.

sections.heading: Save a sequence of designs
steps: In Arrange Pages, tap Select and choose the pages you want. Save as Template preserves those designs in project order.
A single-photo page followed by a two-photo page becomes one reusable two-page template. Add → Add Pages from Template repeats the sequence with your new photos, using this project’s size.
Use Duplicate Page in the page menu, or Duplicate Pages in Arrange Pages, to copy photos and edits within the current project. Panorama panels stay together.
Apply Template to Project changes the existing project’s layouts. Add Pages from Template appends new pages while keeping the current pages.

sections.heading: Start in Templates
steps: Open Templates and tap Create Template. Build the layout with the preview photos, then set its background, frames, text, and optional camera details.
Use Template Preview to try your own photos, show empty photo slots, or preview a repeating batch.
Save and name the template. Preview photos and their photo details are not saved as template content.
To make a template that groups photos by shape, tap Smart Layout instead. See Build your own smart layout.
shots: The Templates tab with Smart Layouts.

sections.heading: Save from a project
steps: In Export, tap Save as Template. Choose pages to include, name the design, and choose whether to include text wording. Photos and crops stay with the project.

Under Photos per Page, choose One per Page, or Group to let photos shaped across the page share one: 2, 3, or Grid of 4, Stacked or Side by Side. By Shape groups any of them; Shape + Time shares a page only between photos taken within 10 minutes of each other. A preview shows how the photos fall.
With Group and more than one page selected, every page uses one page’s design, such as “Every page uses Page 1’s design.”
Your template appears in Templates. Tap Use from Photos in Export for shortcut setup instructions.

sections.heading: Use and manage saved templates
steps: Templates lists Favorites, Smart Layouts, and Your Templates. Tap a template, then choose Use Template to add a new set of photos, or Edit Template to change the design.
Use Template Options to rename, duplicate, share, delete, or use it as your default. Mark favorites to show them first in Templates and in Favorites on Home.
Tap Import Template in Templates to open a shared template file.

macSections.heading: Save a sequence of designs
steps: ⌘-click or ⇧-click pages in the page strip, then Control-click one and choose Save 2 Pages as Template… (the number matches your selection). Decks keeps those designs in project order.
A single-photo page followed by a two-photo page becomes one reusable two-page template. File ▸ Add Pages from Template… repeats the sequence with your new photos, using this project’s size.
Control-click a page and choose Duplicate Page to copy photos and edits within the project, or press ⌘D when no text is selected. Panorama panels stay together.
The Templates menu in the toolbar applies a saved template to this project’s pages. Add Pages from Template… adds new pages while keeping the current ones.

macSections.heading: Start in Templates
steps: Click Templates in the sidebar (⌘3), then Create Template (⌥⌘N). Build the layout with the preview photos, then set its background, frames, text, and optional camera details. New Smart Layout opens the smart layout builder instead.
Click Save Template in the toolbar and name it. Preview photos and their photo details are not saved as template content.

macSections.heading: Save from a project
steps: Choose File ▸ Save as Template… (⇧⌘S). Choose pages to include, name the design, and choose whether to Include Text Wording. Photos and crops stay with the project.
Under Photos per Page, choose One per Page or Group, then how photos share a page and whether to group By Shape or Shape + Time. With Group, every page uses one page’s design.
If a template already has that name, choose Replace Template or Keep Both. Your template appears in Templates.

macSections.heading: Use and manage saved templates
steps: Templates lists Favorites, Smart Layouts, and Your Templates. Click Use Template to start a project with new photos, or Edit Template (Edit Smart Layout for a smart layout) to change the design. To rename a template, edit the name at the top of the window, then click Save Template.
Control-click a template to Favorite it, Set as Default, Export Template…, Duplicate, or Delete…. Favorites appear first.
Click Import Template… to add a template file someone shared, or double-click the file in Finder.

title: Write and copy captions
summary: Prepare posting text for each page.

sections.heading: Write a caption
steps: Tap Caption to write for the current page. Use Preview to review the photo and finished caption together. All Captions opens the project list.
Swipe left or right across the caption workspace, or use the page arrows, to change pages. Your Write or Preview mode stays selected.
Type ; at the start of a word to insert photo information or your saved variables. Review the finished wording for that page.
Captions are separate from text printed on the image. Exporting an image does not paste its caption into another app for you.

sections.heading: Copy as you post
steps: Copy Caption copies the finished wording only. More → Copy with Project Link also includes a link back to Decks.
Use Copy Next in All Captions to copy the next prepared caption. Switch to the app where you’re posting and paste it.
Return to the All Captions for the next page. Copied captions are grouped separately, and pages without captions appear under Needs a Caption.
The More menu lets you arrange pages and reset copied status. You can also reach a project’s All Captions from Projects.

sections.heading: Save captions to Apple Notes
steps: From the Caption screen, open Caption More → Share Markdown, then choose Notes in the share sheet. You can also use Copy Caption and paste the text into a note.
To automate notes for an existing project, connect Decks’ Get Project Captions action to Create Note in Apple Shortcuts. Render Project can provide the finished images for your workflow.

macSections.heading: Write a caption
steps: Open Caption in the inspector to write for the current page. Add Alt Text to describe the image for people using screen readers.
Under Include Photo Details, choose details such as camera or lens to add. Insert Selected Fujifilm Details adds your Fujifilm information.
Save wording you reuse with Save Caption Preset, then choose it from Caption Presets on another page.
Captions are separate from text printed on the image. Exporting an image does not paste its caption into another app for you.

macSections.heading: Copy as you post
steps: Copy Captions copies the captions for every page, in page order. Copy Markdown copies them as Markdown.
Switch to the app where you’re posting and paste.

macSections.heading: Save captions to Apple Notes
steps: Click Copy Markdown in Caption, then paste the text into a note.
Or choose File ▸ Run Workflow…, set Destination to Apple Notes, and click Prepare Workflow. Share the prepared files, or use Copy Text beside each document.
In Apple Shortcuts, Decks’ Get Project Captions action can pass a project’s captions to Create Note.

title: Export your photos & clips
summary: Output settings, saving, sharing, and retries.

sections.heading: Save or share
steps: Open Export in the editor. Pages saves each page as designed; choose all pages or the current page where offered.
Open Export Settings to choose width in pixels, JPEG or PNG, sharpening, and other output settings. JPEG also has quality and file-size controls; projects with video offer video output options.
Review the previews, then tap Save to Photos or Share. Allow Photos access when requested so Decks can save the result.

sections.heading: Metadata and filenames
steps: In Export Settings, choose whether to include location and contact details in the exported file’s metadata.
Use Filename Pattern to control filenames. The listed tokens can insert the original base name, date, page index, or camera information.
Allow Enlarging lets an output grow beyond its normal source-size limit. It does not add detail to a small original.

sections.heading: Keep a project in Projects
steps: Turn off Archive Project After Export if you want the project to remain in Projects after saving or sharing.
Change the default in Settings → Project Cleanup. An archived project is still available under Projects → Archive.

sections.heading: If an export is interrupted
steps: Keep Decks open while a large export finishes. Use Retry Failed when offered; confirmed saves are not repeated.
If Decks asks whether images were saved, check Photos before choosing the saved or retry option.
For a memory error, try a smaller export width or less crop zoom, then retry. Settings → Recent Activity also lists processing runs and available retry actions.

source: Decks source 42c30ae (build 148): reviewed against SocialHelpContentPhone.swift / DecksHelpContent.swift; no build 148 changes to this task.

macSections.heading: Save or share
steps: Choose File ▸ Export… (⇧⌘E), or click Export in the toolbar. Decks exports every page of the project as designed.
Choose JPEG or PNG and an Image Width in pixels. JPEG Quality controls compression; projects with video use the Video Width under Video.
Click Save to Photos, or Export to Folder… to choose a folder. When it finishes, click Reveal in Finder or Share.
Click Continue in Background to keep working while a large export runs.

macSections.heading: Metadata and filenames
steps: Turn Include Location on or off to choose whether location is kept in the exported file’s metadata.
Use Filename Pattern to control the names of exported files.

macSections.heading: Keep a project in Projects
steps: Exporting on your Mac leaves the project in Projects. Archive it yourself when you’re done: Control-click it and choose Archive.
After your first finished export, Decks offers once to save the design as a template. Choose Not Now to skip it.

macSections.heading: If an export is interrupted
steps: If an export fails or you cancel it, click Retry Unfinished Output. Finished files are kept and not repeated.
Recent Activity in the sidebar (⌘5) lists exports with Cancel, Retry, and Reveal Output. If Decks quits during an export, retry it there.
For a memory error, try a smaller Image Width or less crop zoom, then retry. If saving to Photos is refused, allow Photos access in System Settings, or export to a folder instead.

title: Contact Sheet or Proof Sheet?
summary: Export the design, or make an overview of pages.

sections.heading: A Contact Sheet is your design
steps: Choose Contact Sheet on Home to arrange multiple photos together on a page. Keep its film edges, switch to Plain, or choose None.
Open Export to save the sheet as you designed it. You’ll see Your Contact Sheet; each sheet becomes an image. Removing the film border does not change this behavior.

sections.heading: A Proof Sheet is an export option
steps: For other projects, Export offers Pages or Proof Sheet. Choose Pages for the individual finished page designs.
Choose Proof Sheet to make a compact overview of the project’s pages. Open Proof Sheet Details for its options.
You do not need to make a proof sheet to export a Contact Sheet template. Its layout is already the sheet.

macSections.heading: A Contact Sheet is your design
steps: Choose Contact Sheet on Home to arrange multiple photos together on a page. Keep its film edges, switch to Plain, or choose None.
Choose File ▸ Export… to save the sheet as you designed it. Each sheet becomes an image. Removing the film border does not change this.

macSections.heading: A Proof Sheet is an export option
steps: For any project, choose File ▸ Export Proof Sheet… to make a compact overview of its pages.
Choose the Paper, Look, and Film, add a Title or Camera, and choose whether to Use Original Photos and show Filenames. Then click Export JPEG… or Export PDF….
You do not need to make a proof sheet to export a Contact Sheet layout. Its layout is already the sheet.

title: Projects, Archive & Recently Deleted
summary: Find projects and keep your library organized.

sections.heading: Find a project
steps: Projects lists projects by last activity. On iPhone it is the third tab at the bottom; on iPad it is in the sidebar. Tap a project to continue editing; returning Home saves your changes.
Use the project filter in Projects to switch between All Projects, Archive, and Recently Deleted.
Use a project’s actions to rename it, open its All Captions, or manage its place in the library. Pin projects you want to keep out of automatic cleanup.

sections.heading: Understand cleanup
steps: Exported projects can move to Archive automatically. Inactive projects archive after 7 days and move to Recently Deleted after 30 days; pinned projects stay put.

Restore a project from Archive or Recently Deleted when you need it again. Deleted projects are permanently removed after 30 days by default; change the period in Settings, including Never. Original and exported photos are never deleted.
Project cleanup does not delete your original photos or the images you exported to Photos.

macSections.heading: Find a project
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar (⌘2). Switch between grid and list at the top, and use Search Projects to find one by name.
Double-click a project, or select it and press Return, to continue editing.
Control-click a project to Open in New Window, Duplicate, Keep Project, Archive, or Move to Recently Deleted.
Incoming Photos, at the top of Projects, keeps photos sent from Ingest or Shortcuts until you choose a new or existing project.

macSections.heading: Archive and restore
steps: Archived and Recently Deleted are in the sidebar’s Library section. Control-click a project there to Unarchive or Restore it.

Decks on iPhone and iPad archives inactive projects after 7 days and moves them to Recently Deleted after 30; with iCloud sync, you’ll see those changes here. Keep Project keeps a project out of that cleanup.
In Recently Deleted, Delete Permanently… removes a project right away.

Permanently deleting a project also deletes Decks’ copies of its photos and videos, here, on your other devices and in iCloud, unless another project or template uses them. Your Photos library and exported images are untouched.

macSections.heading: Free up space
steps: Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ Storage shows how much space Decks uses on this Mac.
Free Up Space… removes local copies that are safe in iCloud. Opening or exporting a project downloads them again. Media from permanently deleted projects is removed automatically.

title: Sync & Shortcuts
summary: Continue on iPad or reuse a template from Photos.

sections.heading: Sync across Mac, iPhone, and iPad
steps: Decks syncs through your private iCloud account on every device signed in to the same Apple Account. It’s on unless you turn it off in Settings → iCloud.

Sync includes projects, templates, the photo copies those projects need, and your settings: destinations, favorites, favorite places, My Gear, recipes, presets, the last date stamp style you used, and the order of layouts on Home. Appearance stays on each device. Use Sync Now and check the status message if a change hasn’t appeared yet.
Let sync finish before continuing the same project on another device.

sections.heading: Use a template from Photos

title: Install Decks and get started
summary: Join the public beta on iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
body:
Requirements: iOS or iPadOS 18 or later; macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon.

TestFlight is Apple’s app for installing and updating beta apps. You do not need a beta version of iOS, iPadOS, or macOS to use Decks; your device just needs to meet the requirements listed here.

  1. Install TestFlight from the App Store on the iPhone, iPad, or Mac where you want to use Decks.
  2. On that device, open the Decks public beta invitation and choose View in TestFlight.
  3. Accept the invitation if prompted, then choose Install for Decks.
  4. Open Decks and choose your photographs to get started. Return to TestFlight for new builds and beta feedback.

If the invitation opens in a browser after you install TestFlight, open the invitation again on the same device. If TestFlight reports that the beta is full or unavailable, email contact@brianrenshaw.app. See Apple’s TestFlight instructions for installation help.

title: Troubleshooting and feedback
summary: Missing photos, metadata, exports, templates, and sync.
body:
A project disappeared after export

Check Archive. Archive Project After Export can move a saved project out of the main list. On iPhone and iPad, check Settings → Project Cleanup and pin projects you want to keep. Restoring a project is different from recovering a missing original photograph.

Camera or Fujifilm details are missing

Try the original file. Screenshots and edited copies may not contain camera metadata. Fujifilm decoding requires supported original JPEG MakerNotes; a recipe name is supplied by you. Use My Gear or Photo Details for information you know.

An export failed or may have saved twice

Check Photos or the destination folder before retrying an uncertain save. Use Retry Failed on iPhone/iPad or Retry Unfinished Output on Mac when offered. Try fewer pages or a smaller export width after a memory error. Keep Decks running until processing finishes.

Decks cannot save to Photos

Allow the requested Photos access, or review Decks’ Photos permission in the device’s privacy settings. On Mac, Decks → Settings → General includes Allow Saving to Photos. Export to a folder if you do not want to grant Photos saving access.

A project or template has not synced

Confirm the same Apple Account and that Decks iCloud sync is on for both devices. Check the sync status, let media finish downloading, and use Sync Now. Resume paused downloads when appropriate. Sync covers projects, templates, and settings such as destinations, favorites, favorite places, My Gear, Fujifilm recipes, and caption presets. Appearance stays separate on each device.

The Photos list changed while I was choosing

When photos are added to or removed from Photos while you choose, Decks refreshes the list in place and keeps your scroll position and your picks. If a photo you picked is edited in Photos, Decks shows the newer version and you choose it again.

A shortcut cannot find my template

Open Decks and confirm the template is saved. Reopen the shortcut’s action and select an available template. Check that input photos reach Apply Template and that its output connects to Save to Photo Album or Save File.

Send a useful report

Use Send Beta Feedback in TestFlight, or email contact@brianrenshaw.app. Include your platform, OS version, Decks build, the steps you took, and what you expected. Attach only photographs and metadata you are comfortable sharing.
mac: Use Recent Activity to inspect processing jobs. Check Settings → Automation folder access when a file-based workflow fails. Do not assume a missing result means the operation never wrote a file; inspect the destination before retrying.

title: Automate on your Mac
summary: Shortcuts, AppleScript, and the decks command-line tool.
body: On iPhone and iPad, use Decks actions in Apple Shortcuts. See the Photos and Shortcuts guide. The command-line tool, AppleScript, and folder permissions below are Mac features.

macSections.heading: Allow folders first
steps: Open Decks ▸ Settings… ▸ Automation and click Allow Folder… for each folder automation reads from or writes to. Remove takes a folder away.
Files outside an allowed folder return an error instead of opening a window. Shortcuts, AppleScript, and the command-line tool use the same processing and export rules as the app.

macSections.heading: Use the command-line tool
steps: Settings ▸ Automation shows where the decks tool is inside the app. Add its Helpers folder to your shell’s PATH, then run decks --help.

decks templates and decks projects list names with their IDs. decks apply --template ID --output FOLDER followed by files renders them with that template; decks create adds --name and keeps an editable project.
decks render --project ID --output FOLDER exports a saved project. Add --photos to save to Photos, or --async to return the job right away and check it with decks status --job ID.
Results are JSON. The first time, macOS asks to let your terminal control Decks; allow it in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Automation.

macSections.heading: Use AppleScript
steps: Try tell application "Decks" to list templates. Results are JSON with stable IDs.
apply template, create project, and render project start jobs; job status, cancel job, and retry job follow them. open project and project captions work with a project’s ID.
Open Decks’ dictionary in Script Editor for each command’s parameters.

macSections.heading: Use Shortcuts
steps: Decks adds Apply Template, Save Photos with Template, Save Photos and Keep Project, Create Project from Photos, Render Project, Get Project Captions, Open Project, and Add to Incoming Photos to the Shortcuts app.
A typical shortcut is Select Photos, then Apply Template, then Save File or Save to Photo Album.

macSections.heading: Follow your jobs
steps: Recent Activity in the sidebar lists command-line and AppleScript jobs alongside your exports, with Cancel, Retry, and Reveal Output.
Jobs run without opening an editor window. If Decks quits during a job, Retry resumes its saved work.
